subject: SOC 2 applicability by deployment mode — clarification and evidence request
messages:
From: Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: SOC 2 applicability for Dedicated / Private deployments

Hi Marcus,

We are updating our vendor risk file for Redwood and need to confirm which deployment modes are covered by your SOC 2 Type II report for the current audit period (ending 2025-12-31). Specifically:

- Is the SOC 2 Type II report applicable to Hosted API only, or does it also cover Redwood Dedicated reserved pools?
- For customers on Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments, are those in scope of the report or excluded?
- If Dedicated or Private are partially covered, can you point to any boundary diagrams or bridge letters that explain the difference?

Our procurement team is also asking whether you can provide a bridge letter to cover activity between the report end date and today, if applicable.

Thanks — appreciate a short summary and any artifacts we can attach to the questionnaire.

Best,
Tom
Tom Lewis
Head of Vendor Security — Acme Corp

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: SOC 2 applicability for Dedicated / Private deployments

Tom — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer up front: our SOC 2 Type II report and supporting evidence cover the Redwood control plane and hosted inference environment; Dedicated pools are included for controls that Redwood operates and manages, but Private (customer-managed VPC / on-prem) is out of scope for controls that rely on customer-managed infrastructure.

Key points:
- Hosted API: fully in-scope (control environment, change management, access controls, monitoring).
- Dedicated: in-scope for Redwood-managed elements (e.g., our orchestration, host-level patching and kernel hardening we perform when the capacity is provided/owned by Redwood). However, any customer-provided infrastructure or customer-managed network segments for Dedicated co-located in customer spaces are excluded. We document these boundaries in the dedicated-pool boundary diagram (attached).
- Private / VPC / On-prem: out-of-scope for infrastructure-level controls that the customer manages. We provide a list of shared/responsibility split controls that customers must provide evidence for (I can send that matrix).

We can produce a short bridge letter that: (a) states the audit period referenced by the SOC 2 Type II; (b) confirms there have been no material changes to control objectives affecting the hosted and Redwood-managed Dedicated environments since the report end date; and (c) clarifies that Private deployments are not covered by the report and require customer-side attestations.

I'll loop in Dev for the dedicated-pool operational details and Laura for the SOC artifacts. If you can send the exact questionnaire fields that are blocking procurement, we'll attach the relevant evidence and draft bridge letter.

Marcus Lin
Head of Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: dedicated-pool-boundary-diagram.png (png)]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: SOC 2 applicability for Dedicated / Private deployments

Tom — quick technical clarifications from operations:

- Dedicated pools that are hosted and managed by Redwood (reserved GPU capacity in our data centers or cloud accounts where we control the VMs/hosts) are covered by the SOC 2 controls we test. That includes configuration management, secrets handling, and monitoring agents we install.
- For Dedicated where the customer supplies their own hardware or brings-your-own-license (BYOL) instances, those nodes are not covered — we treat those as customer-managed and they fall outside the audit boundary.

I'll also confirm whether any minor infra changes occurred during Q1/Q2 2026 that should be captured in the bridge letter; current visibility suggests no control-affecting changes.

Dev
VP, Infrastructure Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: SOC 2 applicability for Dedicated / Private deployments

Tom — attaching the current SOC 2 Type II (redacted) and a short draft bridge letter for your review. The bridge letter is intentionally conservative: it confirms continuity for hosted + Redwood-managed Dedicated environments and explicitly excludes Private deployments.

Attachments included:
- SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2025.pdf (redacted PII sections)
- draft-bridge-letter-20261005.docx (text-only)
- dedicated-pool-boundary-diagram.png

Notes on evidence: if Acme needs system-level logs from a Dedicated pool that you contracted, we can provide aggregated monitoring screenshots and control reports but not raw customer data. For Private/VPC, your security team will need to supply evidence for things like host patch state and network segmentation.

If the procurement team needs the bridge letter in a signed PDF or on letterhead, say the word and I'll get it routed through Legal.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2025.pdf (pdf)]

From: Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@acme.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: SOC 2 applicability for Dedicated / Private deployments

Laura — this is perfect, thank you. A couple quick follow-ups: please send the signed bridge letter (PDF on letterhead) and the boundary diagram as a high-res image. Procurement will attach the SOC 2 PDF and bridge letter to our questionnaire and accept the redaction.

Also: can you confirm the SOC 2 audit period inside the PDF — I want to ensure our record shows the 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31 testing window.

If possible, please add a one-line sentence to the bridge letter explicitly stating that "No material changes to Redwood-managed control processes impacting Hosted and Redwood-managed Dedicated environments occurred between 2026-01-01 and 2026-10-05." That will satisfy our internal reviewer.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Tom
Head of Vendor Security — Acme Corp
